t: The Crusader army left a well-watered position at La Saphorie against the advice of Raymond III of Tripoli and the Hospitallers, and marched in July heat to a dry plateau where it was surrounded.
Saladin ordered the execution of about 200 Templar and Hospitaller knights and of captured Turcopoles, spared the other captive barons, and had Raynald of Châtillon killed for breaking a truce.
With the field army gone and the castles thinly held, the Crusader kingdom fell quickly, and the defeat led to the Third Crusade.
dyk: Saladin's son al-Afdal, then 17, watched the battle beside his father. He later described how Saladin told him they had not beaten the Franks until Guy's tent fell, and when it fell Saladin dismounted, prostrated himself and wept for joy.
ev: Guy of Lusignan becomes king of Jerusalem in right of his wife Sibylla, over the opposition of Raymond III of Tripoli's faction
Raynald of Châtillon raids a Muslim Hajj caravan during the truce, and in May the Templars are heavily defeated at Cresson
Saladin crosses the Jordan on 30 June and besieges Tiberias on 2 July, where Raymond's wife Eschiva of Bures holds the citadel
On 3 July Guy leaves La Saphorie and marches east, and the army camps without water on the plateau near Meskenah
On 4 July the Crusader army is surrounded and broken, and Guy's tent falls
Saladin has Raynald killed and orders the execution of the captured Templar and Hospitaller knights
Tiberias surrenders on 5 July, and Jerusalem surrenders to Saladin on 2 October
The Third Crusade begins, two years after the battle

f.date: 4 July 1187, after a march that began on 3 July
f.place: Near Tiberias and the village of Hittin, beside the double hill known as the Horns of Hattin, in present-day Israel
f.sides: The Crusader states of the Levant under King Guy of Lusignan, with about 18,000 to 20,000 men including 1,200 knights from Jerusalem and Tripoli and 50 from Antioch; the forces of the Ayyubid Sultanate of Egypt under Sultan Saladin, around 40,000 men including about 12,000 regular cavalry
f.outcome: Most of the Crusader forces were captured or killed. Saladin then took fifty-two towns and fortifications, and Jerusalem surrendered to him on 2 October 1187.
